title: The Pressure Is Up

patient.name: Mr Sim Kah Wai
patient.presenting_complaint: Routine visit — non-contact tonometry shows raised eye pressure, no symptoms

history.hpc: Mr Sim says 'I feel okay, no pain, just come for routine check.' He has no eye symptoms, but his non-contact tonometry readings are high in both eyes.
history.pmhx: No known glaucoma. Family history of glaucoma. No drug allergies.

examination_findings.fundus: For doctor to assess optic discs

investigations.task: Measure IOP correctly with NCT, recognise the raised readings as abnormal, and flag for doctor assessment
investigations.key_points: Normal IOP is about 10–21 mmHg; readings of 28/30 are raised; with a family history of glaucoma and no symptoms, flag for the doctor rather than reassure

diagnosis: Non-contact tonometry shows raised intraocular pressure (28/30 mmHg; normal is about 10–21 mmHg) in an asymptomatic patient with a family history of glaucoma. The OA recognises this as abnormal and flags it for doctor assessment, understanding that glaucoma is often symptomless. No medical diagnosis is made by the OA.

immediate: Confirm identity and perform hand hygiene; wipe the machine contact parts
Ask the patient to remove glasses or contact lenses
Explain that a puff of air will be blown into each eye
Perform NCT, right eye first, and record both readings in mmHg
Flag the raised pressures and the family history for the doctor
Document the readings and the action taken
follow_up: Doctor to assess optic discs and consider visual fields / further glaucoma work-up
Advise the patient to attend follow-up even without symptoms
patient_education: Explain that high eye pressure often has no symptoms but needs checking
Reassure that the doctor will assess further
Stress the importance of attending follow-up given the family history
